text: You crack open a rock... and it is full of animals.
Not fossils. Real animals. Two hundred forty-five, in one rock.
And companies want to dig up billions of these. Here's the catch.
They're called nodules. Potato-sized rocks, four miles down on the Pacific floor.
Scientists opened two hundred forty-four. Over four thousand tiny animals inside.
But they weren't the same animals living in the mud around them. Different neighbors.
So why dig them up? They're packed with metals for batteries.
And the U.S. could approve its first commercial deep-sea mining permit as soon as December.
Which means whole tiny cities could get scooped up... before anyone knows what lives inside.
